solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: We hear he needs people

parts.note: spoken out, 'needs' passes for 'kneads': the clue describes a man who works the muscles of his clients

explanation.surface: Someone overheard admits a man cannot do without other people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' warns that 'needs' must be heard as 'kneads': the man who kneads people is a massage therapist.
explanation.definitionFit: A massage therapist pummels and rubs the bodies of clients, which is kneading people.

clue.text: African politician set upon Lincoln

parts.note: to set upon someone in the street is to mug them
Abe is the familiar name of President Abraham Lincoln

explanation.surface: A politician from Africa launches an attack on a famous American president.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Mugabe was the long-serving leader of Zimbabwe, an African head of state.

clue.text: Sombre at first and dark, but not in shadow

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word sombre is wanted here

parts.note: a dark room is one that is unlit

explanation.surface: A gloomy, dark description that nevertheless claims to be out of the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bathed in sunshine is plainly not lying in shadow.

clue.text: Like an astronaut returning — or failing to get lift-off?

definitions.meaning: a spacecraft heading home is headed for our planet
a rocket that cannot leave the ground stays stuck on the planet

explanation.surface: A space traveller either coming home or stuck on the launch pad.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both heading towards our planet and unable to leave the ground.

clue.text: Bird to take illegally home

parts.note: to rob is to take something unlawfully
someone at home is said to be in

explanation.surface: A bird is told to steal and bring the loot back home.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin is a familiar small garden songbird with a red breast.

clue.text: Log support to sack scoundrel

parts.note: to sack an employee is to fire them
a dog is an old word for a rotten fellow

explanation.surface: A manager weighs up whether to dismiss a villain from the woodyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Firedogs are the pair of metal stands, also called andirons, that hold logs in a hearth.

clue.text: Much activity that could make up for an empty roundabout

definitions.meaning: when things are in their busiest phase they are going at full pelt

definitions.text: that could make up for an empty roundabout
definitions.meaning: by the saying 'swings and roundabouts', what is lost on the roundabout is won on the swings, so a crowded swing compensates

explanation.surface: A playground where a busy ride offsets a deserted merry-go-round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swings and roundabouts' is a British saying meaning losses in one place are balanced by gains in another.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in this state is to be at the height of activity, a common idiom.

clue.text: People in competition

definitions.meaning: a nation or ethnic group of people
a contest of speed, such as a sprint

explanation.surface: Folk taking part in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an ethnic group of humans and a contest of speed.

clue.text: A doctor might mix a gin in medicine

definitions.text: A doctor might mix a gin in medicine

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed inside the word for the measure of medicine

parts.note: a dose is a measured portion of medicine

indicators.note: to mix letters is to stir them into a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor stirring a gin into a patient's prescription.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: identifying an illness is just what a doctor might do, so the wordplay and the meaning are the same sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Identifying an illness from symptoms is exactly what a physician might do at a consultation.

clue.text: Lots of flukes which prevent the balloon going up

definitions.text: Lots of flukes which prevent the balloon going up

parts.words: Lots of flukes which prevent the balloon going up
parts.note: flukes are the barbed arms of an anchor, and small many-armed anchors were used to tether balloons

explanation.surface: A run of strokes of luck that stop disaster striking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flukes' looks like strokes of luck and 'the balloon going up' like trouble breaking out; really they are anchor prongs holding a balloon down.
explanation.definitionFit: These small anchors with several hooked prongs grip the ground, so they can tether a balloon.

clue.text: Ron, e.g., may be one beyond help

indicators.note: says the letters could form something else when rearranged

parts.note: the abbreviation for 'for example', taken as its two letters

explanation.surface: Ron is given as an example of a hopeless case.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone past saving is informally said to be done for, a lost cause.

clue.text: Battle helmet

definitions.meaning: the 1854 Crimean War battle famous for the Charge of the Light Brigade
a knitted woollen head covering leaving only the face exposed

explanation.surface: A soldier's protective headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimean battle gave its name to the knitted head covering worn by troops there.

clue.text: It will enable the pupil to shine

definitions.text: It will enable the pupil to shine

parts.words: It will enable the pupil to shine
parts.note: the pupil is the dark centre of the eye, which gleams when there is radiance in it, not a clever student

explanation.surface: Something that helps a schoolchild do well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupil' suggests a star student; it is the eye's pupil, and 'shine' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiance or luminosity is what makes the pupil of an eye gleam.

clue.text: Unidentified girl accepts ring

indicators.note: the girl's name takes the ring inside it

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A mystery woman agrees to an engagement ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for anonymous, it labels a writer whose name is not known.

clue.text: Sign for a missing letter

parts.note: the punctuation mark that shows where a letter has been left out, as in 'don't'

explanation.surface: A notice put up about a letter lost in the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' suggests post; it is an alphabet letter dropped from a word.
explanation.definitionFit: This punctuation mark stands in for omitted characters in contractions.

clue.text: A dangerous job requires lot of money before final settlement

indicators.note: the first piece comes ahead of the second in the answer

parts.note: something costing a bomb costs a great deal of money
a disposal is a getting rid of, a final settling of affairs

explanation.surface: A risky role that demands a fortune before the deal is closed.
explanation.definitionFit: Defusing and removing explosives is famously one of the most hazardous occupations.

clue.text: Indian food with extra port in America

parts.note: a balti is a spicy curry dish popular in Britain
more means additional or extra

explanation.surface: Ordering a second helping of curry while visiting the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: This Maryland city is a major seaport on the US east coast.

clue.text: Metaphor is mixed but its content is pithy

definitions.note: an adjective standing loosely for the noun: a pithy saying

indicators.note: the letters sought are contained within the words of the phrase

explanation.surface: A writer's tangled imagery that nonetheless expresses something terse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' looks like an anagram signal but is just part of the run of letters; 'its content' points inside the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, memorable saying expressing a general truth is the very model of pithiness.

clue.text: In some danger of finding fault

definitions.meaning: a patient gravely ill is said to be in a serious state

explanation.surface: Someone at risk because they keep complaining.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both gravely serious, as a patient's condition, and inclined to censure.

clue.text: People who believe in one should have their heads examined

definitions.text: People who believe in one should have their heads examined

parts.words: People who believe in one should have their heads examined
parts.note: the jibe 'needs their head examined' is taken literally: this practitioner reads skull bumps

explanation.surface: A scornful remark that believers in someone are mad.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom calls someone crazy; literally, this discredited expert examines heads for bumps to read character.
explanation.definitionFit: This pseudoscientist claimed to read character from the shape of the skull.

clue.text: Maintain there's some body in the beer

indicators.note: the limb is placed inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
a leg is one part of the body

explanation.surface: Claiming there is something solid floating in one's pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some body' looks like 'somebody' but means a part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert or claim something is true is to maintain it, without proof.

clue.text: They have news or distribute it

indicators.note: spreading the letters around gives a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Newspaper proprietors deciding whether to circulate a story.
explanation.definitionFit: Owners are people who possess things, the ones who have them.

clue.text: Decides to change stop

indicators.note: the letters of the word are to be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to alter their halting place on a route.
explanation.definitionFit: To choose one course from several is to make a decision.

clue.text: Cold buffet is a great disappointment

parts.note: a bitter wind is a bitingly cold one
a buffet is a blow or knock

explanation.surface: A chilly spread of food at a party proves a letdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffet' looks like a meal but is a blow, as when wind buffets.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe setback or crushing letdown is idiomatically called this.

clue.text: Head of state moves to centre, showing discrimination

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is the one that moves
the letter is shifted to the middle of the word

explanation.surface: A head of state takes a middle political position, showing judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: Good judgement in matters of style is called discernment or refinement.

clue.text: Payment including king's ransom

indicators.note: the first word holds the letter inside it

parts.note: a fee is a payment for a service
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A fee covering the money demanded for a kidnapped monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ransom' is a verb here: to buy someone's release.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransom a captive is to secure their release, as a verb.

clue.text: Get into debts without interest

parts.note: to incur something, such as debt, is to get into it
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: Falling into debts on which no interest is charged.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking curiosity means showing no interest in things.

clue.text: A bit like audible tranquillity

indicators.note: the word for calm is heard rather than written

parts.note: peace is calm or tranquillity

explanation.surface: Something resembling a little calm you can hear.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment or portion of something is a part of it.

clue.text: The people who got cross during WW2

definitions.text: The people who got cross during WW2

parts.words: The people who got cross during WW2
parts.note: the island nation awarded the George Cross for bravery in 1942

explanation.surface: Folk who became angry in wartime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got cross' looks like 'became angry'; King George VI awarded the whole island the George Cross, a British medal for civilian gallantry.
explanation.definitionFit: The islanders of Malta were collectively given the George Cross during the siege of 1942.

clue.text: Teams of seven put out by the Spanish

indicators.note: the two pieces sit beside each other

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the

indicators.note: the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Sevens sides upset by a Spanish rival.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket and football sides have this many players, so the teams are named for it.
